Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:10:1.english: Who sold his property with the intention of ascending - And he specified to [the buyer] that he was doing [so] with this intention.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:10:2.hebrew: ולא איתדר - ולא יכול לדור — או משום חיסור מזונות, או לא מצא דירה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:10:2.english: And he was not able to settle - And he was not able to dwell [there] — either due to a lack of sustenance, or [because] he did not find a dwelling.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:10:3.hebrew: והא לא מיתדר ליה - והוה ליה כמאן דלא מצי למיסק, והדר זביני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:10:3.english: And behold, he was not able to settle [there] - And he is [considered] like one who was unable to ascend, and the sale is reversed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:11:1.hebrew: אי בעי הוה סליק - ובדידיה קיימא מילתא, ולא בטלה זביניה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:11:1.english: If he wanted, he could have ascended - And the matter depended on him, and his sale is not nullified.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:11:2.hebrew: אי בעי לא סליק - בתמיה: מי אנסו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:11:2.english: If he wanted, couldn’t he have ascended? - [This is stated] as a question: Who forced him?

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:11:3.hebrew: דאיתיליד ליה אונסא באורחא - שמע שהיו ליסטים בדרך. ללישנא קמא, לא הדרינן זביני, דהכי קאמר: דאי בעי למטרח ולאהדורי בתר שיירתא, הוה סליק. וללישנא בתרא, דקא מתמה אתמוהי, ומשמע שלא היה לו שום עיכוב — אבל אם היה לו צד עיכוב, הדרי זביני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:11:3.english: Where circumstances beyond his control arose for him along the way - [For example,] he heard that there were bandits on the road. According to the first version, the sale is not rescinded, for this is what [Rav Ashi] means: that if he had wanted to exert himself and seek out a caravan, he could have ascended. And according to the latter version, which poses [the statement] as a rhetorical question, and implies that [the sale is upheld only because] he had no hindrance whatsoever — but if he had any sort of hindrance, the sale is rescinded.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:12:1.hebrew: אינה מקודשת - דדוקא קאמר ליה מקום פלוני, שיש לי שם אוהבים, ואם בא אדם לומר דברים עלי בפניהם — ימחו בידו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:12:1.english: She is not betrothed - For he specifically told him [to betroth her in] such and such a place, [reasoning:] "I have friends there, and if someone comes to say [disparaging] things about me in front of them, they will protest against him."

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:12:2.hebrew: הרי היא - שם תמצאנה, ואין זו קפידא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:12:2.english: “She is” - [Meaning:] “There you will find her,” and this is not an insistence.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:14:1.english: Here, it was necessary for [the tanna] to teach us [the law of] betrothal - [so] he taught the law of the marriage contract on account of the law of betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:14:2.english: They will not speak words about me - They will not say anything derogatory about me to her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:15:1.english: It is not acceptable for him to degrade himself - For one who divorces his wife, it is a disgrace for him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:16:1.hebrew: תצא שלא בכתובה - דאמר: "אי אפשי באשה נדרנית". אבל גיטא בעיא מדבריהם מספיקא, כיון דלא פריש — דלמא דעתיה נמי אנדרנית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:16:1.english: She is divorced without a marriage contract - For he says: “I do not want a woman who makes vows.” But she requires a bill of divorce by rabbinic decree out of uncertainty, since he did not specify [a condition] — perhaps his intention was also [to accept] a woman who makes vows.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:17:1.english: [The blemishes] that disqualify priests - Are explained in [tractate] Bekhorot (the chapter [entitled] Mumin Elu).

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:18:1.english: Like this - A mishna is taught there, in [the chapter entitled] HaMaddir.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:18:2.english: Here it was necessary for him to teach us [about] betrothal - [He] taught the law of the marriage contract on account of the law of betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:18:3.hebrew: והתם - דקאי בדיני כתובות, איצטריכא ליה משום כתובה, ותנא "המקדש אינה מקודשת" אטו כתובה, דבעי למיתני בסיפא: "כנסה סתם תצא בלא כתובה":
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:18:3.english: And there - Since [the tanna] is dealing with the laws of marriage contracts, it was necessary for him [to teach the mishnah] on account of the marriage contract; and he taught "[If] one betroths... she is not betrothed" on account of the marriage contract, as he needed to teach in the latter clause: "[If] he married her without specifying, she goes out without a marriage contract."

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:19:1.english: Gifts [sivlonot] - Presents that it is customary for a groom to send to his betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:1:1.hebrew: יקריב אותו - קרא יתירא הוא, דהא כתיב ברישא דקרא: ״זכר תמים יקריבנו״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:1:1.english: “He shall offer it” - It is a superfluous phrase, as it is written at the beginning of the verse: “A male without blemish he shall offer it.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:1:2.english: That they coerce him - To fulfill the words of his vow.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:3:1.hebrew: דמצוה לשמוע דברי חכמים - ואית לן לאחזוקיה בחזקת מקיים מצוה, וגמר בלבו לקיים דברי בית דין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:3:1.english: Because it is a mitzvah to listen to the words of the Sages - And we must hold him under the presumption of one who fulfills a mitzvah, and [so] he resolved in his heart to fulfill the words of the court.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:4:1.hebrew: שאני התם דלחומרא - כלומר, איכא למימר: דהא דתני "מקודשת", לחומרא קאמר — שאינה מותרת לאחר בלא גט. אבל קידושין גמורים לא הוו לבטל קידושין אחרים שלא יתפס בה; שאם בא אחר וקדשה, צריכה גט אף משני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:4:1.english: It is different there, since [it is] as a stringency - That is to say, one can say: That which [the Mishnah] taught, "[She is] betrothed," it stated [this only] as a stringency — that she is not permitted to another [man] without a bill of divorce. But it is not a definitive betrothal to negate another betrothal so that [it] would not take effect upon her; for if another [man] came and betrothed her, she requires a bill of divorce from the second [man] as well.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:5:1.english: She is not betrothed - And this is a leniency [so it cannot be dismissed as a stringency].

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:5:2.hebrew: כיון דאתניה - שפירש תנאו בפיו, לאו כל כמינה למיעקר תנאו בדברים שבלב, הואיל ושמעה ולא מיחתה לומר: אעפ"כ אני חפיצה בך, קדש אותי בלא תנאי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:5:2.english: Since he stipulated - That he articulated his condition with his mouth; [therefore,] it is not in her power to uproot his condition with matters [that remain] in the heart, since she heard [him] and did not protest to say: "Even so, I desire you; betroth me without a condition."

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:6:1.hebrew: ורב חסדא הוה בי רב הונא - כלומר, הלך לבי מדרשו של רב הונא לעיין בדבר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:6:1.english: And Rav Ḥisda was in the house of Rav Huna - That is to say, he went to Rav Huna’s study hall to examine the matter.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:6:2.hebrew: הבא לי מן החלון - מעות, והיו שם מעות של הקדש, ושגג בעל הבית, כסבור שהן חולין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:6:2.english: Bring me from the window - [Meaning,] money; and there was consecrated money there, and the homeowner erred, believing that it was non-sacred.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:6:3.english: A box [deluskema] - A bag [Old French: tasche] (tasche: a sack).

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:6:4.english: And he brought [it] to him - From that window.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:6:5.hebrew: לא היה בלבי - מכיס זה, אלא מכיס זה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:6:5.english: It was not in my heart - [To bring] from this purse, but rather from this [other] purse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:6:6.hebrew: בעה"ב מעל - שהרי עשה שליח שליחותו, ותנן (מעילה דף כ.): השליח שעשה שליחותו — הבעה"ב מעל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:6:6.english: The homeowner has committed misuse - For the agent carried out his mission; and we learned in a mishna (Me'ilah 20a): An agent who carried out his mission — the homeowner has committed misuse [of consecrated property].

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:6:7.english: “But doesn’t he say: ‘[It] was not in my heart’?” - And [therefore] it is [a case where the agent] did not fulfill his agency.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:7:1.hebrew: למיפטר נפשיה מקרבן קאמר - ושקורי קא משקר, אבל האי גברא חזינן דטרח לעלות לארץ ישראל ונאנס:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:7:1.english: He says [this] to exempt himself from an offering - And he is lying; but [in the case of] this man, we see that he exerted himself to go up to the Land of Israel and was unavoidably prevented.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:8:1.hebrew: לא עביד איניש כו' - קושיא היא. כלומר: דילמא האי דלא מיפטר, משום דלא מהימן הוא? ודקאמרת: ״היה לו לפטור עצמו בענין אחר, ולומר: מזיד הייתי״ — הא לא ניחא ליה למימר, דמשוי נפשיה רשע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:8:1.english: A person does not [ordinarily], etc. - This is an objection. That is to say: Perhaps the reason he is not exempt is because he is not believed? And as for that which you said: “He could have exempted himself in another manner, and said: ‘I was intentional’” — this, it is not agreeable for him to say, as he makes himself into a wicked person.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:9:1.hebrew: נזכרתי - לאחר (שהלכתי) להוציאה בשוק בשליחותי, נזכרתי שהם של הקדש קודם שהוצאת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:9:1.english: “I remembered” - [The homeowner could have claimed:] “After [you went] to spend it in the marketplace on my mission, I remembered that they were consecrated property before you spent [it].”

Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:9:2.hebrew: שליח מעל - ובעל הבית פטור, דכיון שנזכר לא שגגה היא גביה, ושליח חייב, שהוציא מעות הקדש לחולין. ואילו לא נזכר בעל הבית, הוה רמיא מעילה עליה, דאיתרבי שליח למעול שולחו על ידו בריש פירקין (לעיל קידושין דף מב:). אבל השתא דאיפטר בע"ה, רמיא מעילה אשליח, ככל התורה כולה, דאין שליח לדבר עבירה והעושה הוא מתחייב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50a:9:2.english: The agent has committed me’ilah - And the homeowner is exempt, because since he remembered, it is not [an act of] inadvertence on his part; and the agent is liable, for he spent consecrated money for unconsecrated use. And had the homeowner not remembered, [liability for] me’ilah would have been cast upon him, as an agent was included [by derivation] that his sender commits me’ilah through him, at the beginning of our chapter (above, Kiddushin 42b). But now that the homeowner is exempt, [liability for] me’ilah is cast upon the agent, as in the entirety of the Torah, [which establishes] that there is no agency for a transgression, and the one who performs [the act] is liable.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 50a:11:1.hebrew: דאיתיליד ליה אונסא באורחא - ולעיל, שהוצרך לומר "דברים שבלב אינן דברים", צריך לומר: דללישנא ד"אי בעי לא סליק" — אתיליד ליה אונסא באורחא; וללישנא ד"אי בעי סליק" — צריך לומר דאיתיליד אונס שאפילו ע"י תיור לא היה יכול לעלות:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 50a:11:1.english: "An unavoidable mishap occurred to him along the way" - And [as for the case] above, where [the Gemara] was required to say that "unspoken matters of the heart are not of consequence," one must say: according to the version [that Rav Ashi said,] "If he wanted, couldn't he have ascended?" — an unavoidable mishap occurred to him along the way; and according to the version [that he said,] "If he wanted, he could have ascended" — one must say that an unavoidable mishap occurred such that even by means of a guide, he was not able to ascend.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 50a:8:1.hebrew: היה לו לומר מזיד הייתי - דנהי דאין אנו מאמינים אותו לומר "בלבי היה כך", מכל מקום "מזיד הייתי" הוי טענה מקובלת יותר, ואין נראה כל כך רמאות. והר"ם פי': ודאי "מזיד הייתי" אנו מאמינים לו יותר, כי הא דאמרי' בפ"ק דב"מ (דף ג:) גבי "אמרו לו שנים: 'אכלת חלב', והוא אומר: 'לא אכלתי'", דחכמים פוטרים מטעם דאם ירצה לומר "מזיד הייתי":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 50a:8:1.english: He should have said: "I was intentional" - For although we do not believe him when he says, "It was in my heart [to do] so," nevertheless, "I was intentional" would be a more acceptable claim, and it does not appear to be such deceit. And the Ram [Rabbeinu Meir] explained: Certainly, [if he claimed,] "I was intentional," we would believe him more, like that which we say in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (3b) regarding [the case where] two [witnesses] said to him, "You ate [forbidden] fat," and he says, "I did not eat," where the Rabbis exempt [him] on the grounds that if he wished, he could have said, "I was intentional."
